svg.title: Neighbor-joining tree of single cells from a primary breast tumor and its liver metastasis
svg.desc: Schematic of Navin et al., Nature 472:90 (2011), Fig. 3c. A tree drawn downward from its root at the top; the vertical axis is Euclidean distance from 0 to 6 and the horizontal axis is cell number from 1 to 100. Each leaf is one cell, placed at the depth measured on the published figure; cells from the primary tumor are circles and cells from the metastasis are squares. Cells 1 to 62 hang close to the top, at a distance of about 0.6 to 1: 24 primary diploid, 12 primary pseudodiploid and 26 metastatic diploid cells, mixed together. All the aneuploid cells split off on one long branch, which divides at a distance of about 4.6 into the 22 metastatic aneuploid cells (cells 63 to 84, at about 5.4 to 6.4) and the 16 primary aneuploid cells (cells 85 to 100, at about 6.0 to 6.6). The long branch and its division follow the paper's figure. Inside each group the paper's fine branching is left out and the group is drawn as a comb: one bar with a tooth down to each cell.
